newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed firmer on Wednesday initially shoved by, but subsequently outperforming, German bunds, dealers said.
"We've seen guilders outperform (bunds) after underperformance, especially in the long end," said one trader.
The Jan 2023s ended up 0.25 at 110.88/111.08 and the spread under long bunds widened by two basis points to 20 bp.

Dealers said the morning provided a number of trading opportunities and healthy trading volumes, but that players mostly withdrew during a volatile afternoon, the result of rumours that Russian president Boris Yeltsin had died.
"It was a very volatile afternoon with the rumours of Yeltsin's death," one trader said.
Yeltsin's press office quashed the rumours, saying the Russian President was working at the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow.

The longer end of the bond market was the most active and gains were greatest there. Traders said they had witnessed switching from long-dated Eurobonds into Dutch state loans as well as some purchases from domestic investors at the expense of shorted-dated paper and the money markets to reduce long cash positions.
